source.title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
source.summary: The scaling of LLMs toward long-context inference has shifted the primary serving system bottleneck from computation to memory capacity. Traditional solutions for dense attention models rely on RDMA-based disaggregated memory pools, which perform coarse-grained fetching of the entire prefix KV cache from remote storage to local memory before decoding. However, this approach is fundamentally inefficient for emerging sparse attention models. While only a small fraction of KV entries are active during decoding, these systems still fetch the full KV cache locally, leading to severe transmission bottlenecks and local memory wastage. To address this, we propose SAC, the first efficient disaggregated KV cache system optimized for sparse attention models. By leveraging the low-latency, cache-line granularity load/store semantics of Compute Express Link (CXL), SAC fetches only the required top-k KV entries on demand during inference. Evaluations on DeepSeek-V3.2 using SGLang show that SAC achieves 2.1x higher throughput, 9.7x lower TTFT, and 1.8x lower TBT compared to RDMA-based baselines, establishing CXL-based disaggregation as the superior infrastructure for emerging sparse attention models.

previous_facts.problem: RDMA-based disaggregated KV cache systems perform full prefix cache fetching before decoding, causing transmission bottlenecks and local memory waste for sparse attention models where only a small fraction of KV entries are active
previous_facts.mechanism: CXL-based disaggregated memory with cache-line granularity load/store semantics enables on-demand fetching of only required top-k KV entries during inference

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 2.1x higher throughput compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 9.7x lower TTFT (Time to First Token) compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 1.8x lower TBT (Time Between Token) compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens

evidence.claim: Only 21% of KV cache is actually utilized in 128K-context scenarios for DeepSeek-V3.2
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2, 128K context length, ShareGPT dataset with 1K-token output

evidence.claim: CXL-based disaggregated memory achieves 1.04-1.64x of local DRAM latency for sparse KV retrieval
evidence.condition: Sparse KV indices sampled from 128K-token context, DeepSeek-V3.2 MLA KV entry (512-dim latent + 64-dim RoPE, bfloat16)

previous_facts.evaluation_context: DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse attention model evaluated using SGLang framework across context lengths from 16K to 128K tokens; workload from ShareGPT dataset with 1K-token output; comparisons against RDMA-based disaggregated memory pool and non-disaggregated local memory upper bound
previous_facts.limitations: Evidence limited to abstract/introduction/motivation sections; detailed experimental methodology, hardware configurations, and complete evaluation results not reviewed; CXL memory access pattern results from microbenchmark (Figure 5) not end-to-end serving; specific CXL hardware generation (2.0/3.0) not specified; scalability beyond 128K context not addressed
previous_facts.project_relevance: Directly addresses memory semantics question by demonstrating how CXL's cache-line granularity load/store semantics enable fundamentally different disaggregated memory access patterns compared to RDMA's message-based send/recv model; shows 1.04-1.64x DRAM-equivalent latency for sparse access vs 4.0-19.7x for RDMA; validates CXL mem semantics for fine-grained, sparse KV access; DSA/IAA relevance indirect - work focuses on CXL fabric not CPU offload; end-to-end evidence from SGLang integration with 2.1x throughput, 9.7x TTFT, 1.8x TBT improvements
